content.overview: Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 protects a transferee who has taken possession in part performance of a written contract for transfer of immovable property and has performed or is willing to perform his part. The transferor (and persons claiming under him) is debarred from enforcing against the property any right other than a right expressly provided by the contract, even though the transfer has not been completed in the manner prescribed by law. It is a shield, not a sword, and does not by itself confer title.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Written contract for transfer of immovable property? (2) Possession in part performance? (3) Transferee performed or willing to perform? (4) Shield only — no title?
content.study:
Classic ingredients: written contract; transfer of immovable property contemplated; possession taken in part performance; transferee has done or is willing to do his part.

Post-2001 registration proviso: an unregistered contract required by law to be registered cannot be received as evidence of the contract for the purposes of this section — always check the current official text before pleading.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Shield not sword
sections.body: 53A protects possession; it does not confer ownership or enable the transferee to sue for title on 53A alone.

sections.heading: Written contract
sections.body: There must be a contract to transfer immovable property for consideration, written and signed as required.

sections.heading: Possession in part performance
sections.body: Transferee has taken possession of the property or any part in part performance of the contract.

sections.heading: Willingness to perform
sections.body: Transferee has performed or is willing to perform his part of the contract.

sections.heading: Registration proviso
sections.body: Check current proviso on unregistered contracts required to be registered — evidence bar for this section.

examples.title: Protective possession
examples.body: Buyer under written agreement put in possession, paid/willing to pay price — may invoke 53A as a shield if transferor tries to eject, subject to the registration proviso.

hypotheticals.question: Can the buyer claim ownership solely under s. 53A?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. 53A is a defensive protection against the transferor’s title claim; it does not transfer ownership.

distinctions.title: s. 53A vs s. 54 sale
distinctions.right: Transfer of ownership for price; registered instrument where required.

misconceptions.trap: 53A gives the buyer a title equal to a registered sale.
misconceptions.correction: 53A is a shield only; title still requires a completed transfer under the applicable mode (e.g. s. 54).
